payload.prompt: What does text-to-speech do?

options.rationale: Text-to-speech creates spoken output from text-based data. Its result is audible speech.
This describes speech recognition, which begins with spoken input and produces written text. Text-to-speech works in the opposite direction.
options.better_fit: Use this when spoken words need to become a written transcript.

options.rationale: Mapping phonemes to words is associated with speech recognition. Synthesis starts with text and produces audio.
options.better_fit: This fits a recognition process that interprets speech sounds as words.

options.rationale: Transcription converts recorded speech into text. Text-to-speech generates audio from written content.
options.better_fit: Use this for a voicemail or call that needs a written record.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Text-to-speech converts written content into audible speech.

payload.prompt: Which two items does a text-to-speech solution need?

options.rationale: Speech synthesis needs content to vocalize. The text provides those words.
A voice is needed to vocalize the supplied text. It determines the spoken delivery.
Spoken input is required for speech recognition, not basic text-to-speech. Synthesis starts with text.
options.better_fit: Use this when an app must listen to and interpret a person.

options.error_type: Confuses solution inputs with recognition models
options.rationale: An acoustic model analyzes incoming audio for speech recognition. It is not one of the two required inputs for a text-to-speech solution.
options.better_fit: Use this when recorded or live speech must be analyzed.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Text-to-speech needs written content and a voice.

payload.prompt: Decide whether this statement is true or false.
payload.statement: Speech synthesis generates spoken output from text-based data.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Speech synthesis creates audible speech from text-based data.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This would incorrectly rule out the capability used to make written content audible.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Speech synthesis, also called text-to-speech, generates spoken output from text-based data.

payload.prompt: Decide whether this statement is true or false.
payload.statement: Speech synthesis converts spoken input into written text.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Converting spoken input into written text is speech recognition.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This mixes up a spoken-output task with a spoken-input task.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Speech synthesis converts text into speech, while speech recognition converts speech into text.

payload.prompt: Converting text-based data into audible speech is called ___.

parts.text: Converting text-based data into audible speech is called

payload.explanation: Speech synthesis, text-to-speech, and TTS name the capability that produces audible speech from written content.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The chosen term would describe turning speech into writing instead of making writing audible.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use speech synthesis, text-to-speech, or TTS.

payload.prompt: Order the pieces to state what a text-to-speech solution requires.
payload.explanation: A text-to-speech solution requires both written content and a voice to vocalize it.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The resulting sentence would not clearly identify the two inputs a TTS solution needs.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Start with the TTS solution, then state that it needs text to speak and a voice.

payload.prompt: A retail virtual shopping assistant must read a written order-status update to a customer. Which capability should the developer use?

options.rationale: The update is already written and needs to be spoken aloud. Text-to-speech converts written content into audible speech.

options.error_type: Confuses spoken output with spoken input
options.rationale: Speech-to-text converts a customer's spoken words into text. The need here is to speak an existing written update.
options.better_fit: Use this when a customer says an order number and the app needs written text.

feedback.intrinsic: The customer would not hear the written order update.
feedback.instructional: Use text-to-speech when written content must be read aloud.

options.error_type: Confuses a recognition model with output
options.rationale: An acoustic model helps analyze incoming audio during speech recognition. It does not vocalize written content.
options.better_fit: Use this in the audio-analysis stage of speech recognition.

feedback.intrinsic: The written update would not become a spoken response.
feedback.instructional: Text-to-speech produces outgoing audio; acoustic models help interpret incoming audio.

options.rationale: Call transcription makes written records from spoken calls. It does not generate spoken output from a written update.
options.better_fit: Use this when a support call needs a written record.

feedback.intrinsic: The update would not be delivered as speech.
feedback.instructional: Transcription turns audio into text; text-to-speech turns text into audio.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Text-to-speech can vocalize a written order-status update.

payload.prompt: Which steps are part of speech synthesis?

options.rationale: Synthesis begins by breaking text into individual words. This is tokenization.
Words receive phonetic sounds through phonetic transcription. This prepares them for spoken delivery.
Synthesis creates phonemes before synthesizing audio. These represent the speech sounds used for output.
Mapping phonemes back to words describes the recognition direction. Synthesis moves from supplied text toward audio.
options.better_fit: Use this when recognizing speech from sound representations.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Synthesis moves from text through phonetic processing to audio.

payload.prompt: What does a synthesis system create after processing phonemes?

options.rationale: Speech synthesis turns phonemes into synthesized audio. This is the audible output listeners hear.

options.error_type: Confuses synthesis output with recognition output
options.rationale: Written text is commonly the output of speech recognition. Speech synthesis produces audio.
options.better_fit: Use this when spoken input is being transcribed.

options.rationale: A transcript is written text made from spoken audio. It is not audio created from phonemes.
options.better_fit: Use this for written records of a voicemail or customer call.

options.rationale: A microphone stream is incoming audio used by recognition systems. Synthesis creates output audio rather than capturing it.
options.better_fit: Use this when an app listens to a person in real time.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Phonemes are synthesized as audio.

payload.prompt: Evaluate this statement.
payload.statement: Speech synthesis can organize phonetic transcription into prosodic units such as phrases, clauses, or sentences.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Prosodic units can be phrases, clauses, or sentences.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This would skip the grouping that organizes speech before audio is produced.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Speech synthesis organizes phonetic transcription into prosodic units.

payload.prompt: Arrange the following steps in speech synthesis.
payload.explanation: Speech synthesis starts with text, assigns phonetic sounds, creates phonemes, and then synthesizes audio.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Putting audio before earlier stages breaks the path from text to spoken output.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Follow the synthesis sequence from text, to sounds, to phonemes, to audio.

payload.prompt: The delivery control that determines how quickly synthesized speech is spoken is ___.

parts.text: The delivery control that determines how quickly synthesized speech is spoken is

payload.explanation: Speaking rate controls the speed of synthesized delivery.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The selected term would control a different aspect of delivery or describe another synthesis component.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use speaking rate for the control that determines speed.

payload.prompt: A media producer is tuning an automated spoken announcement and must decide which controls can change its delivery. Which settings should the producer select?

options.rationale: The selected voice affects how synthesized speech is delivered. It is a delivery control for generated audio.
Speaking rate controls speed. Changing it changes how quickly the announcement is delivered.
Pitch controls perceived highness or lowness. It can change the delivery of synthesized audio.

options.error_type: Confuses synthesis delivery with recognition processing
options.rationale: An acoustic model analyzes incoming audio for speech recognition. It is not a delivery setting for synthesized speech.
options.better_fit: Use this when incoming spoken audio is being analyzed for recognition.

feedback.intrinsic: The announcement's voice, speed, and pitch would remain unchanged.
feedback.instructional: Choose voice, speaking rate, pitch, or volume to change synthesized delivery.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Voice, speaking rate, and pitch can change synthesized delivery.

payload.prompt: Which is a use of synthesized speech?

options.rationale: Synthesized speech can vocalize written messages. Reading messages aloud is a direct use of generated audio.
A call transcript is written text made from spoken audio. That is speech recognition rather than synthesized speech.
options.better_fit: Use this when a customer call needs a written record.

options.rationale: Detecting spoken input is a speech recognition task. Synthesized speech generates spoken output.
options.better_fit: Use this when an app needs to listen for what a person says.

options.rationale: Speaker identification analyzes audio to distinguish participants. It does not generate spoken audio.
options.better_fit: Use this when a transcript must identify who spoke each part.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Synthesized speech can read a written message aloud.

payload.prompt: A station is automating its public-address content. Which tasks can be performed with synthesized speech?

options.rationale: Synthesized speech can generate audible replies to user input. It provides spoken output.
Synthesized speech can create audio for public announcements. The resulting speech can be played to listeners.
Transcription converts spoken calls into written text. It does not create an audible reply or announcement.
options.better_fit: Use this for customer-support calls that need written records.

options.text: Identify the language in an audio recording
options.rationale: Language identification analyzes an existing audio recording. Synthesized speech generates new spoken audio.
options.better_fit: Use this when an application must classify the language being spoken.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Synthesized speech can provide spoken replies and broadcast announcements.

payload.prompt: True or false?
payload.statement: Synthesized speech is used to convert customer calls into written transcripts.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Customer-call transcripts use speech recognition.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This would treat a written-record task as though it produced spoken output.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Synthesized speech generates audio; speech recognition converts calls into written transcripts.

payload.prompt: An assistant that generates an audible response to a user's message uses ___.

parts.text: An assistant that generates an audible response to a user's message uses

payload.explanation: Speech synthesis generates spoken replies from text-based content.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The selected capability would process incoming speech rather than generate an audible reply.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use speech synthesis, text-to-speech, or TTS for generated spoken replies.

payload.prompt: Which statements describe the Azure Speech Text-to-Speech API?

options.text: It converts text into audible speech
options.rationale: The API converts text input into audible speech. This is its central purpose.

options.text: It can play audio through speakers
options.rationale: Generated audio can be played through speakers. This is a supported output choice.

options.text: It can write audio to a file
options.rationale: The API can write generated audio to an audio file. This supports later playback.

options.text: It converts microphone audio into text
options.rationale: Converting microphone audio into text is speech-to-text. The Text-to-Speech API takes text and creates audio.
options.better_fit: Use this when microphone speech needs transcription.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. The API creates audio from text for speakers or an audio file.

payload.prompt: Which voice type uses neural networks for more natural sounding speech?

options.rationale: Neural voices use neural networks. They provide more natural speech and improved intonation.
Predefined voices support languages and regional pronunciation. The neural-network feature specifically identifies neural voices.
options.better_fit: Use this when selecting available voices with language and regional-pronunciation support.

options.rationale: Custom voices are developed for use with the API. They are not defined by the neural-network feature stated here.
options.better_fit: Use this when a voice has been developed for the Text-to-Speech API.

options.rationale: Acoustic models help speech recognition analyze audio. They are not Text-to-Speech voice types.
options.better_fit: Use this when discussing speech recognition processing.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Neural voices use neural networks and can improve naturalness and intonation.

payload.prompt: Decide whether this statement is true or false.
payload.statement: Azure Speech Text-to-Speech offers predefined voices with language and regional-pronunciation support.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Predefined voices support multiple languages and regional pronunciation.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This would overlook an available option for matching language and regional pronunciation.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: The API includes predefined voices with language and regional-pronunciation support.

payload.prompt: Order the pieces to describe an API output option.
payload.explanation: The Azure Speech Text-to-Speech API can write synthesized speech to an audio file.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The sentence would not clearly describe the API's file-output capability.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Begin with the API, then state that it can save synthesized speech to an audio file.

payload.prompt: Voices developed for use with the Text-to-Speech API are called ___.

parts.text: Voices developed for use with the Text-to-Speech API are called

payload.explanation: Custom voices are developed for use with the Text-to-Speech API.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The answer would name another voice category or a recognition component.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use custom voices for voices developed for the API.

payload.prompt: A retailer needs spoken product updates in several languages and regional pronunciations. Which Azure Speech voice options can it choose for its Text-to-Speech API solution?

options.rationale: Predefined voices are available through the API. They support multiple languages and regional pronunciation.
Neural voices are available through the API. They use neural networks for more natural sounding speech.
Custom voices can be developed and used with the API. They are an available voice option.
Speech-to-text converts spoken audio into text. It is not a voice option for generating product updates.
options.better_fit: Use this when customer speech needs to become written text.

feedback.intrinsic: The retailer could transcribe speech but could not select a voice for product updates.
feedback.instructional: Text-to-speech voice options include predefined, neural, and custom voices.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Predefined, neural, and custom voices are available for Text-to-Speech.

payload.prompt: What can you choose in the Text-to-Speech Foundry playground?

options.rationale: The playground lets users choose a synthetic voice. That voice is used for generated audio.
A microphone is an input source for speech-to-text. The Text-to-Speech playground starts with text and produces audio.
options.better_fit: Use this in a speech-to-text setting when testing spoken input.

options.error_type: Confuses playground controls with SDK objects
options.rationale: A SpeechRecognizer object is used for speech recognition in code. It is not a Text-to-Speech playground control.
options.better_fit: Use this when writing code that recognizes microphone or audio-file speech.

options.rationale: Batch transcription processes stored audio into text. It does not select a synthetic voice.
options.better_fit: Use this for stored recordings that need transcription results.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. You can choose a synthetic voice in the playground.

payload.prompt: Which delivery settings can be adjusted in the Text-to-Speech Foundry playground?

options.rationale: Speed is an available delivery setting in the playground. It changes the pace of generated audio.
Pitch is an available delivery setting in the playground. It changes perceived highness or lowness.

options.error_type: Confuses delivery controls with audio analysis
options.rationale: Speaker identification analyzes recorded conversation audio. It does not change synthesized delivery.
options.better_fit: Use this when an application must determine who spoke each segment.

options.rationale: Audio transcription produces text from audio. It is not a setting for generated speech.
options.better_fit: Use this when recorded speech must become written text.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. The playground lets users adjust speed and pitch.

payload.prompt: Decide whether this statement is true or false.
payload.statement: The Text-to-Speech playground creates a written transcript from synthesized text.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. The Text-to-Speech playground generates audio output, not a written transcript.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This would expect written notes when the result is meant for a listener.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: The Text-to-Speech playground generates audio from text; transcription produces written text.

payload.prompt: Evaluate this statement.
payload.statement: In the Text-to-Speech playground, users can adjust delivery settings such as speed and pitch.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Speed and pitch are available delivery settings in the playground.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This would miss available ways to change generated speech delivery.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: The playground lets users adjust delivery settings such as speed and pitch.

feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use audio or audio output; the playground generates spoken audio from text.

options.better_fit: Use this when testing how recorded or microphone audio becomes written text.

feedback.instructional: Use the Text-to-Speech playground to adjust voice and speed for generated audio.

options.better_fit: Use this for stored recordings that need transcription results.

feedback.instructional: Batch transcription is audio-to-text work; synthetic voice controls belong in Text-to-Speech.

options.error_type: Confuses text-to-speech with recognition SDK objects
options.rationale: A SpeechRecognizer object recognizes spoken audio in application code. It does not generate spoken audio from written text.
options.better_fit: Use this when writing an application that recognizes microphone or audio-file speech.

feedback.intrinsic: The designer would be set up to listen for speech rather than hear the written sentence.
feedback.instructional: Use the Text-to-Speech playground for generated speech with adjustable delivery.
